posts.title: A chiller swapped over one weekend
posts.excerpt: Pieter de Graaf’s team lifted a new chiller onto the Maasoever energy-centre roof on Saturday morning, and cooling was back on Sunday at 16:00.
posts.content:
On a Saturday morning at Maasoever Office Campus, Pieter de Graaf's team lifted a new chiller onto the energy-centre roof. A mobile crane held the grey machine over the white parapet. Two engineers guided it with tag lines. The offices were empty. Cooling was back on Sunday at 16:00.

Maasoever is six office buildings with a shared energy centre, 58,000 square metres. It has been a Rotterdam site since 2009. The hub is the head office, Maashaven Oostzijde 21, 3072 HK Rotterdam. Pieter is the senior HVAC engineer for plant rooms. The energy centre is the room he is in the note to look after: the pumps and pipe the offices never show. When the chiller that serves that centre is changed, the change is made while the six buildings are empty.

The lift was planned. It was not phoned in as a priority 1 emergency. Priority 1 is reserved for a risk to people, for flooding, or for a total loss of power, heating or cooling. The target on that priority is an engineer on site within two hours, at any hour of any day. A weekend swap sits at the other end of the work. The plant is taken out when there is time to lift it, set it and bring the cooling back before Monday. The desk still knows the job is open. Lucía Ortega's help desk, at the same Rotterdam address, answers +31 10 555 0198 every day of the year.

What the team leaves on the roof is an updated asset record. Readings and photographs go onto the site record, in the same way they do after a reactive visit. The facilities contact receives a closing note the same day. On this job, that note had a simple ending: cooling was back at 16:00 on Sunday. The standing rule, if a part had been missing, is that the return visit is booked before the engineers leave. The rule did not have to be used for a missing part here. It is still the rule on the next job that does.

The ordinary week at Maasoever is meant to be dull. Where a site takes planned maintenance, the contract is a scheduled visit: filters, belts, readings and a quarterly report, from €2,400 a month excluding VAT, for 12 months with three months' notice. A named engineer stays with the site. The weekend lift is not that monthly visit, and this note does not publish a separate price for the crane or the new machine. The only survey fee Hozen prints is €1,850, for one site up to 10,000 square metres, every plant item tagged, with a written report within 10 working days. Maasoever is larger than that band. The 2009 campus was not priced by stretching a figure that does not fit.

Hozen Facilities B.V. was founded in Rotterdam in 1998 by Ingrid Maas, a mechanical engineer, and Kwame Mensah, an electrical engineer. They began with one rented van and a plant room. The work is still plant rooms, roofs, risers and switchrooms, for office campuses and civic buildings between Rotterdam, The Hague and Dordrecht. There are four hubs, 23 contracted sites and 41 engineers. Every contracted site lies within 25 minutes' drive of a hub. That is how the network is drawn. It is not a promise about how quickly a van will reach the gate, and no attendance time in a Hozen contract is anything other than a target.

A fault on another Sunday night would not wait for Pieter's next planned round, and it would not be searched for on the website. It would be a call to the desk. The desk would agree the priority with the caller and text a reference number within 10 minutes. Yusuf Demir leads the out-of-hours rota that covers evenings, nights, weekends and public holidays, the hours from 19:00 to 07:00 and the days when the hubs are not staffed. Hubs themselves are staffed Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 19:00. Head-office hours, for the office as an office, are Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:30. The published first hour on a weekday call-out in that 07:00 to 19:00 window is €95, travel included. The published first hour out of hours is €145, travel included. Each further engineer hour, at any time, is €78. All of those amounts exclude VAT. They are the rate card, not the invoice for this chiller.

The building people see at Maasoever is a courtyard between white offices. The building Hozen is paid to know is the energy centre and the roof. This note records the morning the new chiller went up and the Sunday afternoon the cooling was on again. The facilities contact has the closing note. The next engineer has the asset record. That is the whole of the job, and it is enough.
